title: Planes, trains ... robots and drones? Meet the man who's taking Johnson & Johnson's supply chain into the future
authors: ['Michael Strong', 'as told to Nicole Frehsee Mazur']
summary: Michael Strong, Worldwide Director of Engineering and Packaging for Global Distribution Operations at Johnson & Johnson Supply Chain, is spearheading innovation to modernize the company's delivery of products. He's implementing cutting-edge technologies like "The Hulk" collaborative robot for heavy lifting, augmented reality for faster product picking, and exploring autonomous vehicles and drones for inventory management and urgent deliveries in remote areas. Strong's work aims to enhance efficiency, safety, and customer satisfaction by adopting advanced solutions from factory floor to global distribution.

title: UnitedHealth Group Buys Genoa Healthcare for a Reported $2.5B
summary: UnitedHealth Group has acquired mental health company Genoa Healthcare for a reported $2.5 billion, enhancing its presence in the mental health sector. Genoa, which operates over 425 pharmacies serving behavioral health patients, will be integrated into UnitedHealth's OptumRx pharmacy benefit group. This acquisition comes amidst ongoing merger activity in the healthcare industry and follows Advent International's prior ownership of Genoa.

title: Honeywell to buy German warehouse automation firm Transnorm for $493 million
summary: Honeywell International Inc announced it will acquire Germany-based Transnorm for approximately 425 million euros ($492.8 million) to bolster its presence in the warehouse automation market. Transnorm, which specializes in shipping systems for e-commerce, generates annual sales of about 100 million euros, with a 30 percent growth forecast for the current year. This acquisition follows Honeywell's spin-off of its transportation systems business, Garrett Motion Inc, and its ongoing process to spin off Resideo Technologies Inc.

title: Groupon to pay IBM $57 million to settle U.S. patent dispute
summary: Groupon agreed to pay IBM $57 million to settle a patent dispute over e-commerce technology. This settlement comes after a jury initially sided with IBM, awarding $83 million in damages. The agreement also includes a long-term patent cross-license, allowing Groupon access to IBM's patent portfolio.

title: Rent the Runway CEO: Giving all employees the same benefits is the ‘right thing to do’
summary: Jennifer Hyman, CEO of Rent the Runway, announced a new policy to offer the same benefits to all 1,200 employees, from executives to warehouse workers, including bereavement, parental, family sick leave, and sabbatical packages. She believes this is "the right thing to do" to combat income inequality, even though it will cost the company millions. Hyman aims to disrupt the fashion industry by encouraging clothing rentals over purchases and hopes to eventually put fast fashion retailers like H&M and Zara out of business.

title: Tech Stock Funds Top List Of Best ETFs Over The Past Decade
summary: Tech-focused ETFs, particularly those in biotech, internet, and semiconductors, have dominated the list of best-performing non-leveraged U.S. ETFs over the past decade based on average annual returns. Funds like First Trust Dow Jones Internet (FDN), IShares PHLX Semiconductor (SOXX), and Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) showed strong performance, significantly outpacing the broader market. Leveraged funds such as ProShares Ultra QQQ (QLD) also delivered high returns but come with increased risk and expense ratios.

title: Paying It Forward by Helping Others Do the Same
summary: Rhoden Monrose, founder of CariClub, discusses his journey from benefiting from non-profits as a child to creating a platform that connects young professionals with non-profit board positions. CariClub aims to empower Monrose's generation to engage in philanthropy by matching them with suitable non-profit causes, a mission supported by corporations like Morgan Stanley. Monrose emphasizes the importance of human relationships and passion in entrepreneurial success, drawing lessons from the Morgan Stanley Multicultural Innovation Lab.

title: Target wants to hire 120000 holiday workers, but can it?
summary: Target plans to hire 120,000 seasonal workers for the holidays but faces significant competition from other retailers like Kohl's, J.C. Penney, and Amazon. Amazon recently raised its minimum wage to $15 per hour, potentially complicating Target's hiring efforts as its base pay is lower. This tight labor market poses challenges for Target in securing its desired seasonal workforce.

title: Digital Deals: Amazon backs prefab smart builder, Procore acquires BIManywhere
summary: This article details recent digital deals in the construction technology space, including Procore's acquisition of BIManywhere to enhance its VDC investments and Amazon's significant investment in Plant Prefab, a sustainable smart home builder. It also covers Guardhat's $20 million Series A funding for its smart safety hardhats and a partnership between PCL Construction and Microsoft to develop a cloud-based construction management app.

title: Ross to settle $4.9M lawsuit over ‘deceptive’ price tags
summary: Ross Stores has agreed to a $4.9 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit alleging "deceptive" and "misleading" pricing practices. The lawsuit, filed in 2015, claimed that Ross used false comparative prices on its merchandise tags. This settlement highlights a broader issue of deceptive pricing in the retail industry, which has also affected other major retailers.

title: Upwork shares rocket more than 50% higher at the open on their first day of trading
summary: Upwork's IPO saw its shares rocket more than 50% higher on their first day of trading after pricing its initial public offering at $15 per share, above the expected range. CEO Stephane Kasriel stated the IPO was not about raising money but highlighted the company's mission to connect freelancers with clients globally. Upwork, formed from Elance and oDesk, reported strong revenue growth and addressed fair pay, emphasizing that its business model benefits when freelancers earn more.

title: Amazon to cut stock benefits, production bonuses to warehouse workers, as it raises minimum wage to $15
summary: Amazon announced it will raise its minimum wage to $15 an hour for all U.S. workers, but will simultaneously cut existing stock benefits and production bonuses for warehouse employees. The company stated that while these benefits are being eliminated, compensation will be more "immediate and predictable" with the wage increase, and other benefits like 401(k) and health insurance remain unchanged. This move comes after criticism regarding employee pay, with Amazon encouraging other large employers to follow suit in raising their minimum wage.

title: Amazon drops monthly bonuses, stock grants after minimum-wage hike
summary: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) is raising its minimum wage to $15 an hour but will eliminate monthly bonuses and stock awards for hourly workers to help fund the increase. The company confirmed it is phasing out its stock-grant program and incentive pay, which previously provided two Amazon shares upon hiring and an additional stock option yearly. A single Amazon share is currently valued at approximately $1,952.

title: eBay accuses Amazon of poaching sellers on its marketplace
summary: eBay has accused Amazon of an unlawful scheme to poach sellers from its platform by infiltrating its internal message system. An internal investigation by eBay revealed that Amazon employees were creating accounts and using the member-to-member email system to recruit sellers over several years and continents. eBay has sent a cease-and-desist letter to Amazon, which stated it is investigating the allegations.

title: Costco Wholesale Corp. Q4 2018 earnings
summary: Costco (COST) reported higher-than-expected Q4 sales and earnings, with revenues up 5% to $44.41 billion and net profit reaching $1.04 billion. Despite strong financial performance and membership revenue growth, the stock fell in after-market trading due to the company's disclosure of a "material weakness" in its internal control over financial reporting. E-commerce sales growth, while significant at 26.2%, fell short of expectations amid increased competition.

title: D-Wave Launches Free Quantum Cloud Service
summary: D-Wave Systems Inc. has launched Leap, a free quantum cloud service offering one minute of access per month to its 2000Q quantum annealer, aiming to democratize quantum computing and foster a developer community. This move positions D-Wave alongside IBM and Rigetti in providing online access to quantum hardware, with a focus on ease of use for new developers and the development of real-world applications. The service includes an open-source SDK and a forum for community collaboration, with options for commercial users to purchase additional access.

title: Malicious Component Found On Server Motherboards Supplied To Numerous Companies
summary: Bloomberg reports a bombshell in hardware security: Amazon and Apple allegedly found malicious chips on server motherboards manufactured by Supermicro in China for Elemental Technologies. These tiny, hard-to-spot chips, disguised as signal couplers, may be able to compromise baseboard management controllers (BMCs), providing remote access to servers. While Amazon and Apple deny the claims, the report raises significant questions about supply chain security for high-security applications.

title: Tiny Chinese Microchips Reportedly Found Hidden in Amazon, Apple Servers
summary: A Bloomberg Businessweek report claims that tiny Chinese-made microchips were found hidden in servers used by Apple, Amazon, and government contractors, originating from Super Micro Computer Inc. The chips, allegedly hidden during manufacturing in China, were discovered by Amazon in 2015 and sparked a U.S. government investigation. Both Amazon and Apple have strongly disputed Bloomberg's reporting, denying any such discoveries or investigations.

title: Compromised Supermicro chips reportedly infiltrated US
summary: A Bloomberg report claimed that Chinese government-backed actors infiltrated U.S. companies and government organizations by implanting tiny microchips in Supermicro server motherboards, creating backdoors. Amazon, Apple, and Supermicro have vehemently denied these claims. The article also touches on other cybersecurity news, including a Facebook data breach, Google's new Chrome Web Store rules, and a Telegram vulnerability.

title: Report of Chinese chip implants into servers raises alarm on Capitol Hill
summary: A report alleging Chinese chip implants in servers for companies like Amazon and Apple has caused alarm on Capitol Hill. One representative called for increased scrutiny of supply chains for sensitive electronics from China. The companies implicated, including Super Micro, have disputed the findings.

title: Search company Elastic nearly doubles on first trading day
summary: Elastic (ESTC) saw its stock nearly double on its first day of trading on the New York Stock Exchange, closing up 94.4% at $70 per share. The company, which commercializes open-source software for search and data analytics, raised $252 million in its IPO, pricing shares at $36 each, above its final estimated range. This strong debut occurred on a down day for the broader market, including the tech sector, and contrasts with the performance of other recent tech IPOs.

title: The big hack: How China used a tiny chip to steal data from US companies like Amazon, Apple
summary: Bloomberg reported that China allegedly used tiny malicious chips inserted into computer equipment manufactured for about 30 US companies, including Apple and Amazon, to steal technology secrets. Both Apple and Amazon denied these reports, with Apple stating they conducted rigorous internal investigations and found no evidence to support the claims. The report suggested these chips allowed attackers to create a "stealth doorway" into networks.

title: Retailer of the Year: Kroger Remains Hometown Hero While Radically Transforming the Grocery Business
summary: Kroger has been named Progressive Grocer's 2018 Retailer of the Year for its dual strategy of maintaining its "hometown hero" image while aggressively pursuing innovation and transformation in the grocery business. The company is redefining the customer experience through digital initiatives, strategic partnerships, talent development, and its "Zero Hunger | Zero Waste" social impact program. Kroger's CEO, Rodney McMullen, emphasizes a customer-centric approach, aiming to provide solutions and a seamless shopping experience through various channels, supported by significant investments in technology, talent, and sustainability efforts.

title: Walmart Just Filed for a Weird Patent. Shopping Carts May Never Be the Same
summary: Walmart has filed a patent for a "System and Method for a Biometric Feedback Cart Handle" that could collect shopper's stress levels, body temperature, and heart rate. While Walmart frames this as a way to assist unwell customers, the article suggests the data could be used to optimize store layouts and increase customer spending. The technology raises privacy concerns about how biometric data might be used.

title: Amazon Inaugurates New Tel Aviv Offices
summary: Amazon has inaugurated its new offices in Tel Aviv, located in the Azrieli Sarona tower. The 25,000 square meter space will house various Amazon teams including Alexa shopping, Amazon Web Services, and Annapurna Labs. This expansion solidifies Amazon's presence in Israel, which began with the acquisition of Annapurna Labs in 2015.

title: HPE: Hybrid Cloud Data Protection and Copy Data Management Solutions for Nimble Storage and 3par
summary: HPE has introduced new hybrid cloud data protection and copy data management solutions for its storage portfolio, including Nimble Storage and 3PAR. These solutions aim to enhance operational efficiency, accelerate cloud backups, and reduce storage costs through innovations like the next-gen StoreOnce appliances, Recovery Manager Central 6.0, and integration with Commvault software, all available through consumption-based IT models like GreenLake Backup. The offerings are designed to address the challenges of data growth and evolving SLA requirements by providing intelligent, multi-tiered data protection from on-premises to the public cloud.

title: C3.ai and AWS Expand Collaboration to Drive Enterprise AI Adoption
summary: C3.ai and Amazon Web Services (AWS) have announced an expanded collaboration to accelerate the adoption of complex and strategic AI applications across enterprises. This collaboration builds on the successful deployment of the C3 Platform on AWS by over 30 organizations, focusing on increased investment in customer deployments, joint sales initiatives, and continuous technology integrations. The partnership aims to deliver AI-driven solutions that enable organizations to redefine business processes and gain a competitive advantage.

title: Travelers announces major Amazon partnership
summary: Travelers has announced a partnership with Amazon to offer smart home kits and insurance information through a new "digital storefront" on Amazon.com/Travelers. This initiative includes discounted smart home kits for customers to mitigate common causes of loss, policy discounts for eligible home insurance customers, and new Alexa skills for policyholders and consumers seeking home safety tips. The program aims to innovate and provide value to customers and agents alike, initially rolling out in select US states with plans for expansion.

title: CVS, Aetna merger OK'd by feds, a $69 billion deal to reshape health care
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has approved the $69 billion merger between drugstore chain CVS Health and health insurer Aetna, with the condition that Aetna sells its Medicare Part D prescription drug plan business. This deal aims to significantly reshape health care by integrating CVS's stores, clinics, and prescription drug services with Aetna's insurance coverage, expanding in-store health care offerings. Analysts expect CVS to further evolve into a comprehensive health care hub offering a range of services beyond traditional retail.

title: Insight - Amazon scraps secret AI recruiting tool that showed bias against women
summary: Amazon's secret AI recruiting tool, developed since 2014, was scrapped after it showed bias against women. The system, trained on overwhelmingly male-submitted resumes, penalized resumes containing "women's" and downgraded graduates of all-women's colleges, indicating the limitations and inherent biases that can arise in machine learning when historical data is not neutral. Despite efforts to neutralize specific terms, executives lost hope in the project by 2017, highlighting the challenges in creating fair and unbiased AI for hiring.

title: Walmart acquires online lingerie retailer Bare Necessities
summary: Walmart Inc. announced its acquisition of online lingerie retailer Bare Necessities, marking its second apparel-focused acquisition in less than two weeks. This move is part of Walmart's strategy to attract younger, millennial customers and compete more effectively with Amazon.com Inc. in the online fashion market. Bare Necessities will continue to operate as a standalone brand, with its co-founder overseeing intimates for Walmart's e-commerce platforms.

title: U.S. Credit Card Giants Flout India’s New Law on Personal Data (Published 2018)
summary: Visa, Mastercard, and American Express are flouting a new Indian law requiring them to store all transaction data involving Indian citizens solely on computers within India. This regulation, which came into effect on Monday night, is part of India's "data localization" efforts to gain more control over data and international companies. Despite lobbying efforts and alternative proposals from the credit card companies to store copies of data in India, the Reserve Bank of India has insisted on full compliance and threatened fines.

title: Paul Allen Dies at 65
summary: Microsoft co-founder and former Charter Communications chairman Paul Allen passed away at 65 due to complications from non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. Allen, who co-founded Microsoft with Bill Gates, was also a prominent figure in the cable industry through his purchase of Charter Communications and a dedicated philanthropist. Tributes from Bill Gates, his sister Jody Allen, Michael Powell of NCTA, Senator Patty Murray, Charter Communications, and Jeff Bezos highlighted his impactful career and philanthropic efforts.

title: EBay Owns Just a Slice of the U.S. E-Commerce Market. Here's Why It's Leaning on Brick-and-Mortar Businesses for Help
summary: EBay is implementing a program called "Retail Revival" to help brick-and-mortar small businesses in towns like Akron, Ohio, and Lansing, Michigan, transition to online sales. This initiative comes as eBay faces stiff competition in the e-commerce market and holds a small share compared to giants like Amazon. The program aims to leverage eBay's platform to expand small businesses' reach nationally, offering a lifeline to those struggling against the shift to online retail.

title: New listings: KWEB comes to London
summary: The KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF (KWEB) is expanding its reach by listing in London, following its success in the US market where it has accumulated $1.3 billion in assets. This move positions KWEB, which tracks Chinese internet companies similar to Google and Amazon, as a direct competitor to the Emerging Markets Ecommerce ETF (EMQQ), both of which heavily weight companies like Baidu, Alibaba, and Tencent. The article highlights that KWEB has faced challenges in 2018 with a -17% YTD return due to China's trade tensions and concerns over tech valuations.

title: New listings: KWEB comes to London
summary: The KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF (KWEB), a $1.3 billion fund specializing in Chinese internet companies, has launched in London. KWEB tracks an index focused on overseas-listed Chinese internet firms like Baidu, Alibaba, and Tencent, and boasts a strong five-year performance despite recent challenges. Its arrival in London closely follows another similar ETF, EMQQ, setting up an interesting comparison of two funds with virtually identical fees.

title: Newark NJ's 352 years of history before Amazon HQ2 bid
summary: This article chronicles 352 years of Newark, NJ's history, highlighting key events from its founding in 1666 to its bid for Amazon HQ2 in 2017-2018. It covers significant industrial developments, population changes, social challenges, and major urban revitalization projects. The timeline provides context for the city's ambition to host Amazon's second headquarters.

title: Stitch Fix hit with flurry of lawsuits over growth claims
summary: Stitch Fix is facing multiple class-action lawsuits alleging the styling service made misleading statements about its growth prospects and advertising plans. Shareholders claim the company misrepresented active client growth and the impact of its television advertising on profit and growth. These lawsuits follow concerns from investors about customer retention and acquisition costs, despite initial strong third-quarter results.

title: Adobe XD now lets you prototype voice apps
summary: Adobe XD is integrating voice app prototyping capabilities, powered by its acquisition of Sayspring. This allows designers to create voice-based applications for platforms like Alexa and Google Home, as well as mobile apps with voice input, mimicking real user experiences with voice triggers and speech playback. Additionally, XD is receiving other new features such as a full range of plugins, auto-animate, drag gestures, and deeper integration with Adobe Illustrator and After Effects.

title: Tech Moves: Expedia hires Cortana design lead; Saykara adds VP of growth
summary: This article reports on significant personnel changes in the Pacific Northwest tech community. Sam Moreau, a former Microsoft design leader, has joined Expedia as VP of design operations for the Expedia Group brand team. Additionally, Saykara, a Seattle health tech company, appointed Ryan Plasch as its new vice president of growth, following a recent $5 million funding round.

title: Target to offer more exclusives and activities in first holiday season without ToysRUs
summary: Target is significantly expanding its toy offerings and in-store experiences this holiday season, capitalizing on the void left by Toys R Us's closure. The retailer plans to dedicate more space to toys in over 500 stores, introduce exclusive items, and enhance digital and in-store interactive events to attract shoppers. This aggressive strategy aims to capture a larger share of the $27-billion toy market.

title: Travelers Teams with Amazon to Offer Smart Home Products, Insurance Quotes
summary: The Travelers Companies Inc. has partnered with Amazon to launch a digital storefront offering smart home kits, insurance quotes, and risk management information. This collaboration allows customers to get discounted smart home products and free Amazon Echo Dots (for eligible policyholders), with the aim of advancing Travelers' innovation and risk expertise. Travelers also plans to introduce new Alexa skills to assist policyholders with billing and home maintenance inquiries.

title: Time to Look Under the Hood of Your Alternatives
summary: This article discusses the sudden return of market volatility in October, causing a decline in both stocks and bonds. It highlights the significant drop in FAANG stocks and emphasizes the importance for portfolio allocators to reassess the alternative investment landscape during such turbulent times. The piece focuses on examining structurally diversified alternative investments, excluding commodity, VIX, leveraged, allocation, and tactical funds.

title: Telefonica Brasil Rolls Out Netflix Partnership in Paid TV Push
summary: Telefonica Brasil SA announced it has integrated its pay TV service with Netflix Inc.'s streaming platforms, fulfilling a plan announced earlier in May. This partnership allows customers of both Netflix and Telefonica Brasil's Vivo pay TV service to access Netflix via Vivo platforms. The move is part of Telefonica Brasil's broader strategy to enhance its TV services and aggressive broadband expansion.

title: Merger Creates $70 Million Oracle, SAP and AWS Cloud Consulting Company
summary: Three formerly separate IT businesses—RJT Compuquest, RJT Solution Beacon, and RJT Compusolutions—have merged to form Apolis, an IT staffing, ERP consulting, and cloud solutions company. The new entity boasts $70 million in combined revenues and serves Oracle, SAP, and Amazon Web Services customer ecosystems. Apolis plans to leverage this merger to address emerging opportunities in AI, IoT, and blockchain.

title: ServiceNow sets plans for big expansion in Santa Clara
summary: ServiceNow is planning a significant expansion of its headquarters in Santa Clara, including leasing a new 269,000-square-foot office building expected to be completed in 2021. This expansion reflects the company's rapid growth, with a 28% increase in employee headcount globally in the past year, and is projected to accommodate over a thousand new employees in Santa Clara. The tech company has also extended leases on its existing buildings and currently occupies an additional facility on Jay Street.

title: AI, China, and the Enterprise Covered by Tom Siebel
summary: C3.ai CEO Thomas M. Siebel discussed the profound impact of AI on enterprises, emphasizing its role in solving complex computing problems and optimizing business processes. He highlighted the existential threat to companies failing to adopt AI and expressed concerns about China's formidable advancements in AI, suggesting a competitive "open warfare" scenario.

title: Amazon Is Spending Billions in the Battle to Win Indian Shoppers
summary: Amazon is battling Walmart for supremacy in the Indian online retail market, with both companies investing heavily to attract the country's 1.3 billion customers. Amazon is expanding its reach by partnering with small local kirana stores, turning them into points of contact for villagers to shop online. This strategy highlights the intensity of the competition to capture the growing Indian e-commerce landscape.

title: Global Software Vendors Reap Rewards with Oracle Cloud
summary: Oracle announced that Independent Software Vendors (ISVs) globally are rapidly adopting Oracle Cloud Infrastructure to run their enterprise and cloud-native applications, benefiting from mission-critical performance and security. Leading brands like FICO, FireEye, KNAPP, and Manhattan Associates have publicly endorsed Oracle Cloud Infrastructure for powering their market-leading cloud solutions. This adoption has resulted in quicker time to market, faster customer onboarding, cost savings, and enhanced reliable secure services for ISVs.

title: Caleres snaps up Vionic for $360M
summary: Footwear company Caleres has acquired comfort shoe company Vionic Group for $360 million, expanding its brand portfolio and boosting its presence in the thriving comfort footwear segment. Vionic, which reported $180 million in sales over the last 12 months, will allow Caleres to leverage its existing infrastructure and benefit from Vionic's established management team. This acquisition is seen as accretive to Caleres' earnings and aligns with the growing consumer demand for comfortable and casual footwear.

title: Hasbro results dented by lingering Toys 'R' Us woes, shares drop
summary: Hasbro Inc. missed quarterly revenue and profit expectations due to the lasting impact of Toys 'R' Us's collapse, particularly affecting sales in Europe and the United States. The company is restructuring and retooling its supply chains to adapt to the new retail landscape and changing consumer trends, but shares dropped significantly following the announcement.

title: Arlington approves major changes, additions for Crystal City, including Alamo Drafthouse
summary: Arlington County has approved significant changes and additions for Crystal City, including a new Alamo Drafthouse Cinema. This development is expected to bring a retail infusion to Crystal City, which is a key contender for Amazon's HQ2. The planned Alamo Drafthouse will be a standalone building located between 1550 Crystal Drive and the converted 1770 Crystal Drive.

title: American Express Launches Small Business Card with Amazon
summary: American Express has officially launched its co-branded small business credit card with Amazon, following an earlier partnership announcement. The Amazon Business American Express Card offers rewards and interest-free terms for purchases on Amazon sites, targeting businesses with annual revenues up to $10 million. This product highlights an innovative approach to serving the historically underserved SME market using modern technology.

title: Restaurant Brands (QSR) to Repurchase 10M Class B Exchangeable Limited Partnership Units
summary: Restaurant Brands International Inc. (QSR) and RBI LP announced that 3G Restaurant Brands Holdings LP will exchange over 11 million Class B exchangeable limited partnership units. RBI LP intends to repurchase 10 million of these units for cash and deliver the remaining 1.1 million as common shares of the Company. The cash repurchase will be financed with available cash on hand and will be based on the 20-day volume weighted average price of the Company's common shares.

title: Schwab U.S. Large-Cap ETF
summary: The Schwab U.S. Large-Cap ETF (SCHX) tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Large-Cap Total Stock Market Index, offering exposure to large-cap American companies. It is considered a safe equity play on "Blue Chip" stocks, suitable for investors seeking broad mega and large-cap exposure with low costs. The fund is highly diversified, holding over 750 securities, and can serve as a core building block for many portfolios due to its focus on established, profitable companies.

title: Invesco S&P 500® Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF
summary: This article provides an in-depth profile of the Invesco S&P 500® Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF (RCD), an inactive ETF. It details the fund's vitals, such as its issuer, expense ratio, inception date, and tracked index, along with its classification within the Consumer Discretionary Equities category. The report also covers historical trading data, top holdings, concentration analysis, valuation, dividend information, fund flows, performance metrics, geographic and sector exposure, and technical analysis including volatility and support/resistance levels.

title: Invesco MSCI USA ETF
summary: The Invesco MSCI USA ETF (PBUS) tracks a U.S. large- and mid-cap equity index, excluding small-caps, making it comparable to an S&P 500 ETF. It is part of Invesco’s low-cost PureBeta lineup, offering competitive fees. The fund has attracted significant assets, but its daily trading volume is lower than some longer-established large-cap U.S. equity ETFs.

title: Invesco S&P 500® Downside Hedged ETF
summary: The Invesco S&P 500® Downside Hedged ETF (PHDG) is an actively managed fund designed to provide exposure to rising equities while hedging against market downturns using VIX-linked derivatives. The fund aims to outperform during market declines but may lag during stable bullish periods due to the cost of maintaining VIX hedges. PHDG is priced reasonably for an active strategy, and investors are encouraged to compare its performance against low-cost S&P 500 index funds.

title: Fidelity Nasdaq Composite Index ETF
summary: This page provides a detailed profile of the Fidelity Nasdaq Composite Index ETF (ONEQ), including its price, performance metrics, holdings, expense ratio, and ESG scores. The ETF tracks the NASDAQ Composite Index, offering exposure heavily tilted towards technology and U.S. equities, making it suitable for investors seeking substantial tech sector exposure or as a complementary portfolio holding. It also compares ONEQ's valuation, dividend, and various performance indicators against its peers in the Large Cap Growth Equities category.

title: Invesco S&P 500 Revenue ETF
summary: The Invesco S&P 500 Revenue ETF (RWL) tracks the S&P 500 Revenue-Weighted Index, offering exposure to large-cap U.S. equities like Amazon, Walmart, and Apple, but weighting them by top-line revenue rather than market capitalization. This distinct methodology provides a different risk/return profile compared to traditional cap-weighted funds tracking the same index. While it has slightly higher fees, the ETF is presented as a quality choice for investors who believe in the revenue-weighting system for broad large-cap exposure.

title: MicroSectors FANG+ 3 Leveraged ETNs
summary: The MicroSectors FANG+ Index 3X Leveraged ETN (FNGU) aims to triple the daily return of an index comprising "FANG" stocks and other technology growth companies. Intended for short-term trading by sophisticated investors, its daily rebalancing means its performance can significantly diverge from the underlying stocks. The article also provides detailed financial data, performance metrics, and comparisons to alternative ETFs.

title: Grubhub's COO leaves to become Vivid Seats chief
summary: Stan Chia, formerly the chief operating officer at Grubhub, is moving to become the CEO of Vivid Seats, an online event-ticket reseller. Chia played a significant role in building Grubhub's food-delivery business and will now lead one of Chicago's successful tech companies valued at over $1 billion. This move is seen as a positive development for Chicago's technology community, retaining executive talent within the city.

title: Amplify Online Retail ETF
summary: This page provides a detailed profile of the Amplify Online Retail ETF (IBUY), including its current price, performance metrics, and key holdings. It covers various financial data such as expense ratios, asset under management, dividend information, and ESG scores. The ETF focuses on the consumer discretionary equities sector, specifically broadline retail, with a significant concentration in North America.

title: iShares S&P 500 Value ETF
summary: This article provides a comprehensive profile of the iShares S&P 500 Value ETF (IVE), detailing its price, dividends, expenses, holdings, and performance. It highlights IVE's focus on large-cap U.S. companies with value characteristics, emphasizing its diversification, low expense ratio, and stability benefits for long-term investors. The profile also includes ESG scores, technical analysis, and comparisons to alternative ETFs.

title: First Trust BuyWrite Income ETF
summary: This page provides a detailed profile of the First Trust BuyWrite Income ETF (FTHI), including its price, dividend and valuation, expense ratio, holdings, and performance. It also offers comparisons to alternative ETFs and peer categories, along with ESG scores and technical analysis. The ETF is actively managed and primarily invests in U.S. large-cap blend equities, with top holdings including Apple, NVIDIA, and Amazon.

title: Vanguard Consumer Discretionary ETF
summary: This article provides a detailed profile of the Vanguard Consumer Discretionary ETF (VCR), highlighting its focus on the U.S. consumer discretionary sector and competitive pricing. It includes comprehensive financial data such as holdings, performance metrics, expense ratios, dividend information, and ESG scores. The ETF is presented as a diversified option for investors looking for exposure to consumer spending trends.

title: Global X NASDAQ 100 Covered Call ETF
summary: The Global X NASDAQ 100 Covered Call ETF (QYLD) utilizes a covered call strategy by buying stocks in the Nasdaq 100 index and selling corresponding call options to generate income. This ETF is suitable for investors seeking added yield from Nasdaq stocks with some downside protection, offering an alternative to direct options trading. It provides detailed financial data, performance metrics, and ESG scores for informed investment decisions.

title: D.C. is getting another Canopy by Hilton hotel
summary: Washington D.C. is slated to receive its second Canopy by Hilton hotel, which will replace a Courtyard by Marriott that has operated for two decades. This expansion marks another development in the city's hospitality sector.

title: ProShares Online Retail ETF
summary: This page provides a comprehensive profile of the ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN), detailing its holdings, performance, expenses, and various analytics. It includes information on its top holdings like Amazon and Alibaba, geographical exposure, sector allocation, and real-time ratings. The article also compares ONLN with other ETFs in the Consumer Discretionary Equities category and the Equity: Global Broadline Retail segment.

title: Invesco NASDAQ Internet ETF
summary: The Invesco NASDAQ Internet ETF (PNQI) invests in large, liquid companies involved in internet-related businesses, primarily U.S.-listed but offering global exposure. The ETF significantly allocates to technology and consumer cyclical sectors, targeting firms across various market capitalizations for growth potential. It currently holds top positions in companies like Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, and Microsoft, and has an expense ratio of 0.60%.

title: First Trust Dow 30 Equal Weight ETF
summary: This page provides a detailed profile of the First Trust Dow 30 Equal Weight ETF (EDOW), including its price, performance, holdings, expenses, and ESG scores. The ETF tracks the Dow Jones Industrial Average Equal Weight Index and offers insights into its valuation, dividends, and technicals. It also allows for comparison with other large-cap blend equities ETFs.

title: IBM to Acquire Red Hat for About $33 Billion
summary: IBM announced its acquisition of Red Hat Inc. for approximately $33 billion, marking its largest acquisition to date. This strategic move aims to strengthen IBM's cloud-computing business, which CEO Ginni Rometty sees as crucial for the company's revival. The deal positions IBM to better compete in the evolving cloud market, especially in providing hybrid services that leverage both on-premise and multiple cloud resources.

title: Leonard A. Lauder: In the Game — and Teaching It
summary: This article celebrates Leonard A. Lauder, chairman emeritus of The Estée Lauder Cos. Inc., as the recipient of WWD's John B. Fairchild Honor. It highlights his enduring passion for the beauty industry, his strategic vision in building Estée Lauder into a global powerhouse, and his current role as a mentor and "chief teaching officer." The piece includes an interview where Lauder discusses industry changes, competition, brand acquisition strategies, and his personal philosophies on leadership and philanthropy.

title: Momentum Investing: It Works, But Why?
summary: Momentum investing, a strategy of buying recent stock winners and selling recent losers, has consistently generated above-average returns for decades, challenging the efficient market hypothesis. Despite its proven success, academics, including UCLA Anderson's Avanidhar Subrahmanyam, are still trying to definitively explain why it works. The article explores various behavioral theories, such as investor overreaction or underreaction to information, and calls for more focused research to narrow down the true driving factors.
